body_markdown:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved **Emcitate® (tiratricol)** for adults and children living with **monocarboxylate transporter 8 (MCT8) deficiency** , also known as **Allan–Herndon–Dudley syndrome (AHDS)** . The approval, announced by Egetis Therapeutics on September 28, 2026, marks an important development for people affected by this rare genetic disorder.


According to Egetis Therapeutics, Emcitate is the **first FDA-approved treatment option for MCT8 deficiency in the United States** . The medicine is indicated for the treatment of peripheral thyrotoxicosis associated with MCT8 deficiency in both adult and pediatric patients. It is not recommended for treating primary hypothyroidism.


## What Is MCT8 Deficiency?


MCT8 deficiency is a rare, X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic mutations in the **SLC16A2 gene** . This gene is responsible for producing MCT8, a transporter that plays an important role in moving thyroid hormones into certain cells, including cells in the brain.


When MCT8 does not function properly, thyroid hormone activity becomes disrupted. The central nervous system may receive insufficient thyroid hormone activity, while peripheral tissues can be exposed to excessive levels of the active thyroid hormone **triiodothyronine (T3)** .


This combination creates a complex condition involving severe neurodevelopmental impairment and persistent peripheral thyrotoxicosis.


The disorder can also have effects throughout the body. Elevated T3 levels in peripheral tissues may contribute to a chronic hypermetabolic state involving organs such as the heart, muscles, liver and kidneys. Reported clinical manifestations include failure to thrive, cardiovascular strain, muscle wasting, metabolic imbalance and increased susceptibility to infections.


The source company reports a median life expectancy of approximately 35 years among patients with MCT8 deficiency.


## FDA Approval of Emcitate


Emcitate is a **thyroid hormone receptor agonist** . Under its FDA-approved indication, it is used to treat peripheral thyrotoxicosis in adults and pediatric patients with MCT8 deficiency, or Allan–Herndon–Dudley syndrome.


The FDA approval was supported by a clinical development program that included several studies and programs, including **ReTRIACt, Triac Trial I, Triac Trial II, the Erasmus Medical Center Cohort Study, the EMC Survival Study and the U.S. Expanded Access Program** .


For families affected by MCT8 deficiency, the approval provides access to an FDA-approved treatment specifically indicated for the peripheral thyrotoxicosis associated with the disorder.


## Why This Approval Matters


MCT8 deficiency is a rare condition that can have significant effects on neurological development, metabolism and multiple organ systems. Because of its rarity and complexity, patients often require coordinated care involving specialists familiar with thyroid disorders, genetics, neurology and other areas of medicine.


The FDA approval gives physicians in the United States an approved treatment option for managing peripheral thyrotoxicosis associated with MCT8 deficiency.


Egetis Therapeutics said its immediate focus following approval is helping eligible patients obtain access to Emcitate. The company expects the medicine to become commercially available in the United States approximately **eight to ten weeks after approval** , according to its announcement.


## Egetis RareLink Patient Support Program


Alongside the FDA approval, Egetis announced the launch of **Egetis RareLink** , a patient support program designed to assist eligible patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals with access to Emcitate.


The company has partnered with **PANTHERx Rare** as part of its U.S. commercialization strategy. According to the announcement, the partnership is intended to support medication access, education, care coordination and ongoing treatment services.


Egetis has also established specialty distribution and dedicated support resources as part of its planned access infrastructure.


## Priority Review Voucher Granted


The FDA also granted Egetis a **Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV)** in connection with the approval of Emcitate.


The company stated that it expects to explore the potential monetization of the voucher, potentially during the fourth quarter of 2026. However, the timing and outcome of any transaction remain subject to market conditions.


## Important Safety Information


Emcitate carries a boxed warning stating that it is **not for the treatment of obesity or weight loss** .


The FDA-approved information also lists **primary hyperthyroidism as a contraindication** .


During treatment initiation and dose titration, patients receiving Emcitate may experience signs and symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. These can include increased heart rate, elevated blood pressure, diarrhea, excessive sweating, irritability, insomnia and nightmares. The prescribing information states that patients should be monitored and that the dose should be adjusted when appropriate.


Another important consideration involves laboratory testing. Tiratricol can cross-react with certain immunoassays used to measure T3, potentially producing unreliable or overestimated T3 results.


The most common adverse reactions reported in the source material, occurring in at least 5% of patients, include **diarrhea, vomiting, rash and hyperhidrosis** .


Patients and caregivers should discuss the medicine, potential risks and monitoring requirements with their healthcare professional.


## What the Approval Means for the MCT8 Community


The approval of Emcitate represents a new treatment development for people in the United States living with MCT8 deficiency. It also highlights the importance of research into rare genetic diseases for which treatment options have historically been limited.


Early diagnosis remains important because MCT8 deficiency is a complex disorder requiring specialized evaluation and coordinated care. The availability of an FDA-approved treatment may give healthcare professionals another option when managing peripheral thyrotoxicosis associated with the condition.


As access to Emcitate develops in the United States, patients, caregivers and clinicians will need to work together to understand eligibility, treatment requirements, monitoring and support services.


### Source


Egetis Therapeutics announcement regarding the FDA approval of Emcitate (tiratricol) for MCT8 deficiency.
